title: ATLAS Bootstrap-to-Platform Roadmap
purpose: Turn the current local control-plane bootstrap into a self-extensible operating platform that a non-technical user can install once and then configure, extend, supervise, and improve primarily through the ATLAS dashboard.
operatingPrinciples: Build one complete vertical capability at a time.
Every visible control must use real application state or explain why it is unavailable.
Agents report only through their environment Manager.
The Development Assistant evolves ATLAS itself and does not dispatch operational work.
Sensitive actions require scoped permissions, audit records, and human approval.
Connected environments initiate outbound authenticated connections; ATLAS does not expose raw machine or browser debugging ports to the internet.
No milestone is complete until type checking, linting, unit tests, integration tests, and an end-to-end smoke test pass.

milestones.title: Complete the real local execution loop
milestones.objective: Make a Manager-defined workflow execute real, permissioned tools on the connected laptop and produce verified results.
deliverables: Typed environment tool registry and execution broker
Per-Manager and per-agent permission scopes
Correct temporary-agent creation at run start and retirement at terminal state
Workflow run, pause, resume, cancel, retry, and disable controls
Bounded retries, timeout handling, recovery state, and artifact capture
Independent result verification with evidence
A real disk-space workflow executed from the dashboard
acceptance: The user starts the disk-space workflow from the dashboard.
The Manager deploys a temporary agent with only the required system-information permission.
The agent retrieves real disk-space values through the tool broker.
The Manager verifies the values, reports the result, logs the run, and retires the agent.
completionEvidence: Dashboard disk-space action invokes the typed local tool broker.
Temporary agent receives only system.disk.read permission.
Real disk values are independently reconciled and stored as a verified artifact.
Run lifecycle supports pause, resume, cancel, one bounded retry, timeout failure, and workflow enable/disable.
Manager audit records completion and temporary-agent retirement.

milestones.title: Dashboard-operated platform settings
milestones.objective: Remove normal provider, secret, diagnostic, and runtime configuration work from manual files and terminals.
deliverables: Settings area for model-provider and model selection
Encrypted secret-reference store with create, rotate, test, and revoke operations
Provider connection tests and honest error reporting
ATLAS service status, restart, diagnostics, backup, and recovery controls
Environment permissions and capability management
Unavailable controls with actionable explanations
acceptance: A non-technical user can configure and test Groq or another provider without editing .env.local.
Secret plaintext is never stored in the application database, prompts, logs, or audit details.
Routine ATLAS administration no longer requires a terminal.

milestones.title: Secure environment connector protocol
milestones.objective: Separate environment execution from the control plane so local and remote physical environments can be enrolled safely.
deliverables: Installable environment runtime
Device identity, enrollment, revocation, and exactly-one-Manager assignment
Outbound encrypted real-time connection to the control plane
Signed commands, short-lived capability grants, and replay protection
Offline buffering, reconnection, heartbeats, and recovery
Remote capability, health, workload, and capacity reporting
acceptance: A second computer can be enrolled without opening an inbound debugging or command port.
ATLAS can revoke the environment and prevent further commands.
Interrupted connections recover without losing or duplicating execution events.

milestones.title: Remote active-browser connection
milestones.objective: Allow a Manager to supervise approved browser tabs in an active local or remote browser session.
deliverables: Local browser bridge or extension
Explicit browser-session and tab-scoped consent
DOM, accessibility, navigation, screenshot, download, and error observation
Controlled click, type, select, scroll, and navigation tools
Persistent connected indicator, immediate disconnect, and revocation
Redaction of passwords, cookies, unrelated tabs, and sensitive fields
Complete Manager-owned browser action audit
acceptance: The user connects one chosen browser tab from a physical environment.
The Manager can inspect and operate only that approved tab.
Disconnecting or revoking the session immediately prevents further access.

milestones.title: Task observation and workflow learning
milestones.objective: Let a Manager observe the user completing a task, infer a reusable workflow, and report every required asset and permission.
deliverables: Teach by observation and hybrid instruction-plus-observation modes
Visible recording scope and consent controls
Semantic action and state-transition capture
Sensitive-field, notification, clipboard, and unrelated-window redaction
Workflow graph inference with decisions, waits, errors, and recovery paths
Asset, account, secret, tool, capability, and permission requirements report
User correction and approval editor
Safe rehearsal mode before autonomous activation
acceptance: The user records one browser-based workflow.
The Manager produces an editable workflow and requirements report.
ATLAS replays the workflow in rehearsal mode and identifies deviations.
The workflow cannot become autonomous until the user approves it.

milestones.title: Development Assistant engineering loop
milestones.objective: Make platform evolution from inside ATLAS reliable, reviewable, test-driven, and recoverable.
deliverables: Multi-step repository inspection and context gathering
Bounded implementation plans tied to roadmap milestones
Transactional multi-file edits with previewed diffs
Automated checks, failure analysis, correction loops, and regression tests
Rollback when verification fails
Decision records and roadmap status updates
User-facing implementation report and remaining-risk summary
acceptance: The user starts a roadmap milestone from the dashboard.
The Development Assistant inspects, implements, tests, and presents the verified change.
All material writes and commands remain scoped, auditable, and approval controlled.

milestones.title: Authentication, remote control plane, and mobile readiness
milestones.objective: Securely expose ATLAS state and HITL controls beyond the host computer and prepare the Android client contract.
deliverables: User authentication, sessions, roles, and device enrollment
Versioned API and real-time event stream
Remote HITL notifications and idempotent decisions
Emergency pause and environment isolation
Android-ready generated API contracts
Reconnect-safe state synchronization
acceptance: A second authenticated device receives live state and approval events.
Approvals cannot be replayed or duplicated.
A disconnected client recovers without missing material events.

milestones.title: Android supervisory client
milestones.objective: Provide secure mobile monitoring, Manager conversation, task deployment, HITL, and emergency control.
deliverables: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose application
Environment, Manager, workflow, run, and capacity views
Manager conversations and task deployment
Push notifications and biometric approval confirmation
Pause, cancel, and emergency isolation controls
Audit and verified-result views
acceptance: The Android client securely connects without duplicating ATLAS business logic.
The user receives and resolves a real HITL request.
Revoking the device immediately removes access.

milestones.title: Production hardening and installer
milestones.objective: Make ATLAS safely installable, recoverable, observable, and maintainable for non-technical users.
deliverables: Signed installer and automatic local service setup
Secure updates with rollback
Database migration backup and recovery testing
Resource, cost, and rate-limit controls
Security review, abuse controls, and threat-model remediation
Operational documentation and first-run guidance
acceptance: A clean machine can install and launch ATLAS without development tools.
An interrupted update rolls back safely.
A backup can restore environments, Managers, workflows, audit history, and non-secret configuration.
